name: desire to improve
description: Wanting to make yourself or the situation better in a particular way.

comparisons.description: Gaining knowledge is a special form of improving yourself or your situation. Having a healthy body and mind requires knowledge, desire, and effort over time.

guidance.description: There's no shortage of guides to help you improve things: getting in shape, dealing with social problems, fixing machines, handling garden weeds, playing the guitar, stress management, etc.

variations.name: desire to improve your environment
variations.description: Dissatisfaction with some aspect of your physical, social, or existential environment that prompts you to want to make a change.
perceptions: Some part of my environment is not ideal.
results: Try to find a way to improve the environment
examples: Calling someone to fix the dishwasher.
Wanting to live in a clean place with safe water.
Wanting to stay away from people who are perceived to be a bad influence.

variations.name: desire to improve the self
variations.description: Engaging in physical exercise, study, or meditation toward improving your physical or mental health.
perceptions: My body or mind could be better.

variations.name: desire to improve skills
variations.description: Spending time in practice toward improving skills.
perceptions: It would be good for me to be more skilled in this area.

variations.name: desire to improve existential self
variations.description: Engaging in physical exercise, study, meditation, or moral behavior with the goal of narrowing a perceived gap between your actual and ideal self.
perceptions: I'm not living in accordance with my highest ideals.

commentaries.quote: Optimizing things to be 'better' is the absolute core of being a 'civilized' human trying to live in a ridiculously complicated world. All that effort is why we get so upset when things get 'worse'. But either we do this, we regress to the jungle, or we join a mountaintop monastery.

We always optimize towards a goal. Most of the time the goals we quest for are unconscious, so it may be worth reflecting on your favorites. Some common ones: fortify economic stability, have fun, feel better about myself, enhance my social status, prepare for the afterlife, make the world fit into an ideology, etc.
There is only one corner of the universe you can be certain of improving, and that's your own self.
You must have a level of discontent to feel the urge to want to grow.
To change the world takes time; to change yourself takes courage.
Start now. Optimize later. Imperfect starts can always be improved.
If you optimize everything, you will always be unhappy.
